proof.text: Use Mathlib ProfiniteGrp.limit and its limitConeIsLimit to obtain the continuous homomorphism on compatible families. Its coordinate formula is definitional. The existing construction already supplies compact Hausdorff topological group structures on both limits.

For each compatible c in C, form the Type-valued functor of fibres {x in I_j | theta_j(x)=c_j}. Naturality gives its transitions, and functoriality follows from that of I. Each fibre is finite and nonempty by component surjectivity. Apply nonempty_sections_of_finite_inverse_system to obtain a compatible lift. This nonemptiness theorem needs no surjectivity of the fibre transitions, so the kernel adjustment in the original plan is unnecessary.

Coordinatewise equality with the identity proves ker(theta)=P. Its closedness follows by continuity as the inverse image of the closed identity singleton. Transport normality along this kernel equality. Compose quotientMulEquivOfEq with quotientKerEquivOfSurjective to obtain the group equivalence I/P -> C; the quotient-map continuity criterion proves it continuous, and Continuous.continuous_symm_of_equiv_compact_to_t2 proves the inverse continuous. Evaluation on cosets is definitional.

For a continuous surjective f:P -> Q with Q finite discrete, its kernel is an identity neighbourhood. Expand the two subtype neighbourhood filters and the product neighbourhood filter to find finitely many coordinate neighbourhoods whose cylinder is contained in the kernel. Directedness, by induction on this finite set, produces an index j mapping to all these coordinates. Compatibility shows that any element with j-coordinate one has all restricted coordinates one, hence lies in ker(f). Thus ker(pi_j) <= ker(f). This includes the empty finite set, using the nonempty index type.

Let pi_j:P -> P_j be coordinate evaluation. Its range is a subgroup of the finite p-group P_j, and pi_j.rangeRestrict is surjective. The kernel inclusion descends f to a homomorphism phi:range(pi_j) -> Q by MonoidHom.liftOfSurjective. Its defining equation and surjectivity of f prove that phi is onto. Apply IsPGroup.of_card to the stated order of P_j, IsPGroup.to_subgroup to its projection image, IsPGroup.of_surjective to phi, and IsPGroup.exists_card_eq with the given primality hypothesis. No surjectivity of pi_j is required.

lean.statement: theorem finiteExtension_inverseLimit_exact_pro_p {Λ : Type u} [PartialOrder Λ] [Nonempty Λ] [IsDirectedOrder Λ] (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (I C : Λᵒᵖ ⥤ ProfiniteGrp.{u}) [∀ j : Λᵒᵖ, Finite (I.obj j)] [∀ j : Λᵒᵖ, Finite (C.obj j)] [∀ j : Λᵒᵖ, DiscreteTopology (I.obj j)] [∀ j : Λᵒᵖ, DiscreteTopology (C.obj j)] (P : ∀ j : Λᵒᵖ, Subgroup (I.obj j)) [∀ j : Λᵒᵖ, (P j).Normal] (hPorder : ∀ j : Λᵒᵖ, ∃ n : ℕ, Nat.card (P j) = p ^ n) (θ : I ⟶ C) (hθsurj : ∀ j : Λᵒᵖ, Function.Surjective (θ.app j)) (hθker : ∀ j : Λᵒᵖ, (θ.app j).hom.toMonoidHom.ker = P j) (hIsurj : ∀ {j k : Λᵒᵖ} (f : j ⟶ k), Function.Surjective (I.map f)) (hCsurj : ∀ {j k : Λᵒᵖ} (f : j ⟶ k), Function.Surjective (C.map f)) (hPsurj : ∀ {j k : Λᵒᵖ} (f : j ⟶ k), (P j).map (I.map f).hom.toMonoidHom = P k) : (∀ (x : limit I) (j : Λᵒᵖ), (finiteExtensionLimitMap θ x).val j = θ.app j (x.val j)) ∧ Function.Surjective (finiteExtensionLimitMap θ) ∧ (finiteExtensionLimitMap θ).toMonoidHom.ker = finiteExtensionLimitKernel I P ∧ IsClosed (finiteExtensionLimitKernel I P : Set (limit I)) ∧ (∃ hnormal : (finiteExtensionLimitKernel I P).Normal, ∃ e : @ContinuousMulEquiv (limit I ⧸ finiteExtensionLimitKernel I P) inferInstance (limit C) inferInstance (@QuotientGroup.Quotient.group (limit I) inferInstance (finiteExtensionLimitKernel I P) hnormal).toMul inferInstance, ∀ x : limit I, e (QuotientGroup.mk x) = finiteExtensionLimitMap θ x) ∧ (∀ (Q : Type v) [Group Q] [Finite Q] [TopologicalSpace Q] [DiscreteTopology Q] (f : finiteExtensionLimitKernel I P →ₜ* Q), Function.Surjective f → ∃ n : ℕ, Nat.card Q = p ^ n)
